newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, uncertainty continues.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, uncertainty continues.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.75 percent on Wednesday on continued uncertainty and market participants said they expected to see volatility in the market over the next few weeks.
"I think we will have to have strong nerves as market will be volatile in the short term," Davor Dubokovic, a trader at Eastbrokers said.

The 11-share SBI index tumbled 10.79 points to 1,430.3, falling for the second day in a row in technical correction after two days of strong gains. Overall five shares fell, eight rose, one was unchanged and 11 were untraded.
Turnover dropped to 235.3 million from 442.3 million.
"Turnover will probably continue falling until some fresh information and reactions to last week's move by the central bank are available," Dubokovic said
Last week the Bank of Slovenia said that international investors would have to open special custody accounts at one of the country's 14 fully licenced banks in order to trade in Slovenian securities.
The bank later said the measure was taken to regulate foreign portfolio investment.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share, firming 5.17 percent to 61,000 tolars on volume of 2,353 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, falling 3.70 percent to 13,000 tolars on volume of 56 shares.
Warehouse operator BTC was the biggest gainer, rising 6.58 percent to 14,100 tolars on volume of 366 shares for total turnover of 5.1 million tolars.
